messages.author: 20b73f4748706290
messages.subject: plotmath for xlab()
parts:
Hello:

I am wondering how to put "red blood cell (*10^6)/micro L" (note:
"micro" should be Greek small mu symbol) in the xlab().

Thanks a lot.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: plotmath for xlab()
parts:
d <- data.frame(x = 1, y = 1)
ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() +
   xlab(expression(paste("red blood cell (*10^6)/",mu, "L")))

HTH,
Dennis

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: plotmath for xlab()
parts:
Hi:

Here are some possibilities:
d <- data.frame(x = 1, y = 1)
ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() +

xlab(expression(paste("red blood cell"%*%10^6,"/",mu, "L")))

although I might prefer cell to be plural :) The reason the original %*% didn't work is because the operator needs both a left and right argument, and only the left one was given. The text string 'red blood cell' provides the needed left argument.

# (2) Another possibility (my preference):
ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() +

xlab(expression(paste("red blood cells (",10^6, "/",mu, "L)")))

# (3) My initial stab at this was to use phantom, which works if its argument is an empty string, and contains the multiplication sign:
ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() +

xlab(expression(paste("red blood cell (", phantom()%*%10^6,")/",mu, "L")))

Hopefully, one or more of these work for you...

Dennis
